overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 1
overview.pill: Module 3 • Use Properties of Operations to Generate Equivalent Expressions
overview.text: In this lesson on Generating Equivalent Expressions, explore proportional reasoning, rational number operations, algebraic equations, or geometric proofs aligned with national Common Core standards.
outcomes: Develop conceptual understanding and fluency with Generating Equivalent Expressions.
Apply properties of operations and proportional reasoning to formulate models and equations.
Demonstrate precision in problem solving and communicate mathematical reasoning using clear mathematical notation.
overview.teacherInsight: Emphasize the transition from visual tape diagrams and double number lines to formal algebraic equations ($y = kx$, $p + q$, $I = Prt$). Guide students to verify their solutions by substituting values back into original expressions.

vocabulary.definition: The constant value of the ratio between two proportional quantities, typically denoted by $k = \frac{y}{x}$.
Any number that can be expressed as the quotient or fraction $\frac{p}{q}$ of two integers, with the denominator $q \ne 0$.
The number that, when added to a given number, yields zero ($a + (-a) = 0$).

problemSet.description: Work through these curriculum problem set exercises for Generating Equivalent Expressions. Record your steps in the digital workspace and check with the teacher solutions.

problems.title: Problem 1: Simplifying Linear Expressions
problems.prompt: Expand and simplify the algebraic expression: $4(2.5x - 3) - 2(1.5x - 8) + 7x$. Collect all like terms.
problems.problem: Expand and simplify the algebraic expression: $4(2.5x - 3) - 2(1.5x - 8) + 7x$. Collect all like terms.
problems.hint: Apply the distributive property first, paying careful attention to distributing the negative sign in $-2(1.5x - 8)$.

problems.title: Problem 2: Two-Step Inequality & Graphing
problems.prompt: Solve the inequality $-3x + 15 \le 36$. State the solution set and describe its graph on a number line.
problems.problem: Solve the inequality $-3x + 15 \le 36$. State the solution set and describe its graph on a number line.
problems.hint: Subtract $15$ from both sides. When dividing by a negative number, remember to reverse the inequality symbol.
problems.solution: $-3x \le 36 - 15 \implies -3x \le 21$. Dividing by $-3$ reverses the symbol: $x \ge -7$. The graph features a solid closed circle at $-7$ with shading extending to the right.

problems.title: Problem 3: Circle Area & Circumference
problems.prompt: A circular garden has a diameter of $14\text{ feet}$. Using $\pi \approx \frac{22}{7}$, compute both the circumference and the area of the garden.
problems.problem: A circular garden has a diameter of $14\text{ feet}$. Using $\pi \approx \frac{22}{7}$, compute both the circumference and the area of the garden.
problems.hint: Radius $r = \frac{d}{2} = 7\text{ ft}$. Use $C = 2\pi r$ and $A = \pi r^2$.

practiceQuestions.explanation: Grade 7 mathematics emphasizes rigorous proportional relationships, rational operations, and linear equations.

problems.problem: Expand and simplify the algebraic expression: $4(2.5x - 3) - 2(1.5x - 8) + 7x$. Collect all like terms.
problems.hint: Apply the distributive property first, paying careful attention to distributing the negative sign in $-2(1.5x - 8)$.

problems.title: Problem 2: Two-Step Inequality & Graphing
problems.prompt: Solve the inequality $-3x + 15 \le 36$. State the solution set and describe its graph on a number line.
problems.problem: Solve the inequality $-3x + 15 \le 36$. State the solution set and describe its graph on a number line.
problems.hint: Subtract $15$ from both sides. When dividing by a negative number, remember to reverse the inequality symbol.
problems.solution: $-3x \le 36 - 15 \implies -3x \le 21$. Dividing by $-3$ reverses the symbol: $x \ge -7$. The graph features a solid closed circle at $-7$ with shading extending to the right.

problems.title: Problem 3: Circle Area & Circumference
problems.prompt: A circular garden has a diameter of $14\text{ feet}$. Using $\pi \approx \frac{22}{7}$, compute both the circumference and the area of the garden.
problems.problem: A circular garden has a diameter of $14\text{ feet}$. Using $\pi \approx \frac{22}{7}$, compute both the circumference and the area of the garden.
problems.hint: Radius $r = \frac{d}{2} = 7\text{ ft}$. Use $C = 2\pi r$ and $A = \pi r^2$.
